investigation.question: Why did Invoke-Cell in run_phase7_grid.ps1 never launch V5 and V4-conflict?
confirmed: No log file exists for either cell at the grid's launch stamp (no logs/phase7_V5_20260909_020855.log, no logs/phase7_V4-conflict_20260909_020855.log), even though Invoke-Cell unconditionally appends to $script:Results after every attempt -- the manifest entry with ExitCode=2 proves the function body ran to completion for both cells.

Empirically reproduced on this machine (Windows PowerShell 5.1, the version this repo runs on): `Invoke-Expression <cmd> 2>&1 | Tee-Object -FilePath $LogPath` creates $LogPath only once it receives at least one pipeline object. A native command that exits non-zero after producing ZERO stdout -- even if it writes to stderr, which 2>&1 nominally merges in -- causes Tee-Object to receive nothing and never create the file. Verified directly: `python -c "import sys; print(1,file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(2)"` run through the exact Invoke-Cell pattern leaves no log, exit=2 -- reproducing V5/V4-conflict's signature exactly.

src/eval/harness.py's main() only emits its first stdout line (`torch.cuda.is_available() = ...`) AFTER argparse.parse_args() succeeds. Zero stdout is therefore consistent with a failure at or before argument parsing / Python startup -- not a crash mid-run (mid-run would have flushed at least the cuda-status line and any harness prints before dying, and Minutes would not read 0.0).
ruled_out: argparse rejecting --variant V4-conflict as an invalid choice: VARIANTS in src/eval/harness.py already registers 'V4-conflict' (used for resolve_variant / scoring), so it is a valid --variant value. Also would not explain V5's failure, which passes no --variant flag at all.

A PowerShell parse error in the command STRING itself: both commands are plain space-separated CLI invocations, structurally identical to V1/V3's (which succeeded from the same $H template) and V4-conflict's own --variant token, differing only in the config path / trailing --variant value.
investigation.leading_hypothesis: Resource exhaustion on the 15 GB machine (ADR-037's own documented OOM history), not a code defect in either cell. B3 (the immediately preceding cell) ran 207.7 minutes with OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1, so Ollama's 7B model stayed resident the entire time; V5 and V4-conflict are the two heaviest remaining cells (agents + calibration, agents alone) and need to load the retrieval stack (dense/BM25/cross-encoder models) on top of that resident model. Python's stdout is block-buffered (not line-buffered) when piped rather than attached to a real console, exactly Invoke-Cell's situation -- so an abrupt process kill (OS-level OOM) before the buffer's first flush would lose ALL buffered output, including the cuda-status line, leaving zero stdout: consistent with the confirmed Tee-Object behavior above, the zero-stdout evidence from harness.py's print ordering, and the fact that only the two most memory-hungry cells, run back-to-back right after the longest prior cell, were the ones affected.
investigation.not_certain: The OOM hypothesis is not independently verified (no OS-level crash log was captured at the time, and it cannot be reproduced now without repeating the exact memory conditions of that night, which would mean rerunning scoring code -- out of scope here). It is reported as the leading, evidence-consistent hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause.
investigation.fix_applied: run_phase7_grid.ps1's Invoke-Cell now writes a one-line stub log (cell name, command, timestamp) via Set-Content BEFORE invoking the command, so a future zero-stdout failure still leaves a log file to inspect, and a follow-up 'child process was terminated' probe ($LASTEXITCODE plus $Error[0] if the pipeline itself faulted) is appended after the attempt. See docs/05_DECISIONS.md ADR-039.
